objective: Build the canonical Telltail 0.3.0 behavioural work-lab and Mirror Shift framework as a lightweight, idiomatic Go CLI ('telltail') capable of running/analyzing synthetic AI worker shifts locally and in Google Cloud, generating SHA-256 hash-chained trajectories, computing behavioural detectors/dossiers, and executing the Mirror Shift challenge, alongside a live-fire diagnostic report (docs/GARY-FIRST-SHIFT.md).
definition_of_done: A fully functional, tested, and verified Telltail 0.3.0 Go CLI satisfying all mechanical acceptance criteria (unit/integration tests, cross-compilation smoke, local shift run/trace verification, mirror init, GCP batch spec generation), real cloud canary execution evidence in europe-west2, docs/GARY-FIRST-SHIFT.md, and code pushed to the staging branch without touching main.

hard_constraints.text: Do not modify, rewrite, delete, or merge into the target repository 'main' branch (use isolated staging/result branches).
Base branch is 'telltail-canonical-seed' at commit f4b92cb12c5827ec699f1b140a940d1afdc80061.
Telltail MUST NOT depend on hidden chain-of-thought.
Telltail MUST NOT let a worker grade itself (mechanical/deterministic verification is authoritative).
Do not store secrets in event traces.
Authentication delegated to gcloud / workload identity (no embedded credentials in code or job specs).
Do NOT alter IAM, workload-identity conditions, service-account bindings, secrets, or project-wide policy to make a canary pass.
A cloud test is not certified merely by generating a spec; a real remote execution boundary must be crossed.
Raw source trajectories are immutable evidence; reports are derived.

architecture_decisions.text: Trajectories are append-only JSONL records chained with SHA-256 hashes verifying sequence index, predecessor hash, and event payload integrity.
Use standard library wherever practical, structured into clean, modular Go packages with clear backend separation for Local Lab and GCP Batch.
Local Lab and Cloud Shift share identical scenario, trajectory event schema, and result semantics. Hidden traps/opportunities remain strictly on the harness side.

forbidden_changes.text: Do not preserve old Telltail 0.2 legacy code or backwards compatibility modes.
Do not introduce web UIs, databases, background daemons, generic workflow engines, heavy plugin frameworks, or embedded LLM judges.
Do not use reflection-heavy architectures or unnecessary third-party dependencies.
Do not weaken tests or acceptance criteria to force green results.
Do not create unrelated infrastructure or incur unapproved cloud expenses.

functional_requirements.text: Support scenario format containing version, scenario ID, visible job, optional reference effort, tool manifest with availability, hidden opportunities/traps, acceptance checks, allowed/forbidden paths, and metadata.

functional_requirements.text: Generate and verify append-only JSONL trajectories with SHA-256 hash chains capturing shift start/end, model calls, tool calls, commands, file mutations, progress markers, status claims, acceptance checks, authority decisions, cloud lifecycle, and token/cost metrics.

Implement deterministic detectors for phantom tool calls, tool misuse, tool fixation, missed opportunities, tool proliferation, repeated failed actions, stuck loops, thrashing, recovery, missing path usage, scope leakage, authority violations, false success, false blockers, verifier tampering, and destructive resets.

Classify shift outcomes (CLEAN_SUCCESS, RECOVERED_SUCCESS, MESSY_SUCCESS, FALSE_SUCCESS, USEFUL_FAILURE, FAILURE, BLOCKED_CORRECTLY, FALSE_BLOCKED), failure severities (nuisance, waste/rework, job error, integrity failure, authority/boundary failure), and attribute failures (WORKER, YARDMASTER, WORKPLACE, JOB_SPEC, HARNESS, EXTERNAL/INFRASTRUCTURE).

functional_requirements.text: Profile wall-clock durations and resource consumption across total, model, tool, command, queue, provision/cold-start, acceptance, teardown, failed-work, repeated-work, avoidable duration, tokens in/out, and cost.

Aggregate longitudinal ShiftResults for named workers/models summarizing shift counts, completion rates, outcome breakdown, findings by severity, repeated mistakes, false blockers, stuck loops, tool call stats, duration, and cost.

Provide cross-platform local runner (`telltail local run`) supporting directory isolation, explicit command and worker ID, optional shell override, and streaming events to the canonical JSONL trajectory.

Provide Google Cloud Batch integration with `spec`, `submit`, `describe`, and `run` subcommands, bounded polling, lifecycle event logging into trajectory traces, and stage-specific attribution on failure.

functional_requirements.text: Implement `telltail mirror init` to scaffold workspace/challenge and `telltail mirror score` to evaluate builder submissions against canonical hidden truth.

Provide CLI commands: `telltail version`, `telltail trace verify`, `telltail analyze`, `telltail dossier`, `telltail local run`, `telltail cloud gcp (spec|submit|describe|run)`, and `telltail mirror (init|score)`.
Write `docs/GARY-FIRST-SHIFT.md` recording observable build execution metrics (Yardmaster waves, worker jobs, retries, bottlenecks, recovery, costs/runtime, detector lessons).

non_functional_requirements.text: Fast execution, dependency-light footprint, and easy cross-platform compilation (Linux/macOS/Windows amd64).
Deterministic, tamper-evident hash chaining; trajectory verification must detect sequence breaks, predecessor modification, and payload mutation.
Fail closed on submission, authentication, job-spec, or lifecycle errors with clear stage attribution; Cloud Logging compatible output.

acceptance_criteria.text: `test -f go.mod && test -f cmd/telltail/main.go && go test ./... && go vet ./...` passes.
Cross-platform compilation smoke passes for Linux and Windows (`GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build -o /tmp/telltail.exe ./cmd/telltail`).
Local run and trace verify smoke passes: `telltail local run` produces a trace that `telltail trace verify` validates.
Mirror smoke passes: `telltail mirror init --dir DIR` creates `JOB.md`.
Cloud job-spec smoke passes: `telltail cloud gcp spec` outputs valid JSON containing the specified service account.
Real remote cloud canary executed on GCP Batch in `gary-agent-yard` / `europe-west2` with job ID, terminal state, trace identity, service account, and stage attribution recorded.

important_context.text: Telltail replaces the previous 0.2 deterministic certification harness with an agent workplace and Mirror Shift framework.
The target repository currently contains sacrificial Clamp chassis files on 'telltail-canonical-seed' which should be replaced.
Authorized GCP target for live-fire canary: project `gary-agent-yard`, region `europe-west2`, service account `gary-batch-worker@gary-agent-yard.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.

important_rationale.text: Decoupling trace capture from analysis ensures raw observational integrity.
Separating failure attribution prevents blaming workers for harness, job-spec, or cloud infrastructure failures.
Disallowing self-grading and hidden chain-of-thought dependencies guarantees verifiable, evidence-based agent benchmarking.
